title: EigenQ and Silicon Valley Acquisition Corp. Advance $3B SPAC Merger via Form S-4 Submission - Quantum Computing Report
gist: EigenQ and Silicon Valley Acquisition Corp. (Nasdaq: SVAQ) confidentially filed a draft Form S-4 with the SEC, advancing their de-SPAC merger that values EigenQ's post-quantum cryptography and hardware-rooted trust business at ~$3.0 billion, with closing targeted for Q4 2026 under the ticker EIGQ.

insights.claim: EigenQ, Inc. and special purpose acquisition company Silicon Valley Acquisition Corp. (Nasdaq: SVAQ) have confidentially submitted a draft registration statement on Form S-4 to the SEC, a formal regulatory step toward completing their previously announced business combination, which values EigenQ at a pro forma enterprise value of approximately $3.0 billion.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Confirms the de-SPAC is progressing on schedule; investors in SVAQ shares should track SEC review timing as the next catalyst before the ticker converts to EIGQ.

insights.claim: Upon SEC review, effectiveness of the registration statement, and shareholder approval, the combined entity will be renamed EigenQ Holdings, Inc. and list its common stock on Nasdaq under the ticker "EIGQ," with closing targeted for the fourth quarter of 2026.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Gives investors a concrete timeline and ticker to track for the public listing event.

insights.claim: EigenQ's initial commercialization targets NIST-compliant post-quantum cryptography (PQC), hardware-rooted trust, and quantum-derived entropy designed to satisfy federal directives, including CNSA 2.0 mandates.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Positions EigenQ's near-term revenue thesis around mandatory federal PQC compliance timelines rather than long-horizon quantum computing itself, a differentiated, sooner-to-monetize angle versus pure-play QPU makers.

insights.claim: EigenQ's platform integration and distribution rely on strategic channel and OEM partnerships with HPE, AMD, WNC, and TD SYNNEX.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Named enterprise and hardware partners suggest an existing go-to-market channel already in place ahead of the public listing, reducing commercialization risk relative to peers without such alliances.

insights.claim: Texas-headquartered EigenQ is led by CEO Dr. José Rosas-Bustos and Board Chairman Dr. Jesse Van Griensven, with the transaction remaining on track for an anticipated close in Q4 2026.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Names the decision-makers relevant for tracking future strategic announcements from the combined entity.
